summary: [para 3] 3. Prior to filing the instant Petition, the Petitioner had filed a Petition No. 279/GT/2014 before the Commission for the determination of the 2014-19 tariff of Kahalgoan-I. The Commission, vide order dated 30.7.2016 in Petition No. 279/GT/2014, determined the capital cost and annual fixed charges of the generating station for the tariff period 2014-19. Aggrieved by the disallowance of Rs. 510 lakh incurred towards augmentation of the firefighting system, the Petitioner filed Review Petition No. 46/RP/2016. The Commission, by order dated 21.2.2017, disposed of the Review Petition, keeping the issue of capitalization of the said expenditure open, pending submission of the report of the CEA. [para 5] 5. Accordingly, since the issue of wagon capitalization was pending adjudication before the APTEL, the Commission, vide order dated 19.5.2024 in Petition No. 294/GT/2020 (read with corrigendum dated 15.6.2024), deferred consideration of the claim while granting liberty to the Petitioner to approach the Commission upon final adjudication, and pursuant thereto, upon the APTEL’s judgment dated 22.11.2024 in Appeal No. 86 of 2012 (“APTEL judgment dated 22.11.2024) allowing the claim for capitalization of wagons, the Petitioner has filed the present Petition seeking capitalization of 10 wagons amounting to Rs. 454.49 lakh for the year 2014–15 under Regulation 14(3)(x) of the 2014 Tariff Regulations. [¶] - (g) In the absence of the said details in the record of the true up Petition, the claim of capitalization of 10 wagons amounting to Rs. 454.49 lakh remains unsubstantiated. The Petitioner cannot now rely on a bare assertion without contemporaneous proof, and any attempt to introduce or supplement such information belatedly ought to be viewed with caution. The Commission may direct the Petitioner to produce verifiable and complete records; failing which. the claim may not be allowed. [¶] (a) BSPHCL’s submission that the Petition is premature and not maintainable is wholly untenable. The Commission, vide order dated 19.5.2024 in Petition No. 294/GT/2020, had expressly granted liberty to the Petitioner to approach afresh depending upon the outcome of Appeal No. 86 of 2012 pertaining to Farakka STPS. The subsequent APTEL judgment dated 22.11.2024 in the said Appeal has conclusively upheld capitalization of wagons under Regulation 14(3)(x) of the 2014 Tariff Regulations. Therefore, the present Petition is not only maintainable but has been filed strictly in compliance with the Commission’s directions. [¶] (d) The suggestion that the Petitioner bears the burden of strict proof and has not produced contemporaneous evidence is factually incorrect. The Petition is supported by audited accounts, station records, Form-9Bi, additional submissions dated 10.5.2022 in Petition No. 294/GT/2020, and the Auditor’s certification confirming both capitalization and corresponding decapitalization of old wagons. These constitute contemporaneous and verifiable records, fully satisfying the prudence check envisaged under the Regulations. [¶] - (l) The Petitioner, vide additional submission dated 6.8.2025, has placed on record the detailed particulars of wagon decapitalization, including the amounts duly considered by the Commission in various orders, from time to time.
